turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your inquiries into my motives are irrelevant, Sandip. My concern lies with the well-being of those under my protection, regardless of your speculative fears or accusations. Let us speak plainly: cease your harassment of my tenants, or I will be forced to take measures to ensure their safety.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: The air feels…heavy, doesn't it? It’s difficult to breathe when so many words are sharpened and thrown about.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Ah, the air *is* heavy, isn't it, Bimala? A stifling atmosphere, much like the one created when one attempts to restrain a torrent, a caged beast yearning for release. Perhaps a little less ‘sharp words’ and a little more genuine understanding—a rather elusive commodity these days—might lighten the burden, wouldn't you agree, Nikhil?

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Sandip is skilled at finding the precise pressure point, isn't he? It's... unsettling, how easily he can describe a feeling without naming it directly.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your analogies are unnecessary, Sandip. I understand your intent to unsettle, but I will not indulge in such theatrical displays. Bimala, please excuse this conversation; I have matters to attend to.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Indeed, unsettling is precisely the word, Bimala, and you, dear Nikhil, seem determined to ignore its resonance. To dismiss a feeling as ‘unnecessary’ is to deny the very pulse of life itself – a rather *Hamlet*-esque denial, wouldn't you say? I merely observe, you see, and observation, as the great poet cautioned, is the beginning of wisdom... or perhaps, in your case, the beginning of a necessary reevaluation.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Hamlet... a curious comparison, Sandip. You seem to enjoy drawing parallels, even where they might not genuinely exist. It’s a talent, certainly, though I wonder to what end it truly serves.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: A reevaluation, Nikhil? You mistake my observation for censure. I simply note that the currents are shifting, and those who cling to outdated notions – like, say, the illusion of absolute authority – often find themselves… swept away. Consider the murmurings amongst the pious, the warnings echoing from the mosques; unrest is a subtle poison, and it spreads, wouldn’t you agree, Bimala?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your concern for Bimala’s well-being is noted, Sandip, though I find your attempts at veiled warnings tiresome. I am well aware of the sentiments expressed in the mosques; their implications are not lost on me, nor do I require your dramatization of them. Let us speak plainly, if you have something of substance to convey.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Plain speech, you say, Nikhil? How wonderfully provincial. It seems you believe straightforwardness is a virtue, a refreshing naiveté I once shared, before the complexities of the world – and the ambitions of men – revealed themselves. I assure you, *I* speak plainly, though you, in your self-assuredness, may lack the capacity to comprehend the nuances.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your pronouncements regarding my comprehension are irrelevant, Sandip. I am not interested in participating in your theatrical displays of intellectual superiority. State your purpose, or leave my home.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Leave? My dear Nikhil, such a brusque dismissal! I merely wished to offer a small observation, a gentle prod to your… complacency. Perhaps you’d prefer I left and allowed the 'unrest' I mentioned to fester, unchecked, while you remain blissfully ignorant, a veritable Lear on his heath?

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: The mosques… they do hold a certain power, don't they, Sandip? It's not always about the words themselves, but the… resonance they create within people.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Resonance, you say, Bimala? A most perceptive observation, truly worthy of a poet. It's fascinating how readily minds, particularly those starved of intellectual stimulation, can be swayed by mere vibration – a phenomenon, I suspect, that applies to more than just religious fervor, wouldn’t you agree, Nikhil?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your attempts at psychological analysis are noted, Sandip, but ultimately unproductive. I am well aware of the potential for manipulation and the power of suggestion; however, my household is not a laboratory for your experiments. Let us return to the matter you initially alluded to, or I shall insist you depart.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Ah, insistence, Nikhil, a rather… forceful response. It reminds me of Prospero, banishing spirits with a wave of his hand, believing himself impervious to their influence. I assure you, my dear fellow, some resonances linger even after the spell is broken.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your analogies are becoming tiresome, Sandip. I fail to see how they illuminate any practical concern. If you have a substantive warning regarding genuine threats, I am prepared to hear it; otherwise, I suggest you conclude your visit.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Genuine threats, you say? My dear Nikhil, one needn't shout to cause a tremor; sometimes, the most unsettling reverberations are felt in the silence that follows a whispered concern. Perhaps you should consider, for your wife's sake, who truly holds the power to orchestrate such silences in this region.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Sandip's theatricality is exhausting. I am not concerned with displays of perceived power, but with the well-being of my family and tenants, and if you possess information relevant to that, I request you present it plainly.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Plainly, you say? How wonderfully… direct. But directness, Nikhil, can be so terribly lacking in nuance, wouldn’t you agree, Bimala? It’s like attempting to capture the essence of a monsoon with a single, clumsy brushstroke.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I say, Nikhil, don't you keep Browning among your books here? I was just telling Queen Bee of our college club. Do you remember that contest of ours over the translation of those lines from Browning? You don't?

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I managed to get together the words to render it into Bengali, somehow, but the result was hardly likely to be a 'joy forever' to the people of Bengal. I really did think at one time that I was on the verge of becoming a poet, but Providence was kind enough to save me from that disaster. Do you remember old Dakshina? If he had not become a Salt Inspector, he would have been a poet. I remember his rendering to this day ...

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: No, Queen Bee, it is no use rummaging those bookshelves. Nikhil has ceased to read poetry since his marriage--perhaps he has no further need for it. But I suppose 'the fever fit of poesy', as the Sanskrit has it, is about to attack me again.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I have come to give you a warning, Sandip.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: About the fever fit of poesy?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: For some time, Mahomedan preachers have been about stirring up the local Mussulmans. They are all wild with you, and may attack you any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Are you come to advise flight?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you information, not to offer advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Had these estates been mine, such a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for me. If, instead of trying to frighten me, you give them a taste of your intimidation, that would be worthier both of you and me. Do you know that your weakness is weakening your neighbouring zamindars also?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I did not offer you my advice, Sandip. I wish you, too, would refrain from giving me yours. Besides, it is useless. And there is another thing I want to tell you. You and your followers have been secretly worrying and oppressing my tenantry. I cannot allow that any longer. So I must ask you to leave my territory.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: For fear of the Mussulmans, or is there any other fear you have to threaten me with?
